day_shape: 47 items: Araghchi lands in New Delhi for BRICS foreign ministers' meeting, White House issues NDAA §1245(d) presidential determination on Iran oil sanctions, Iran executes Ehsan Afrashteh for alleged Mossad espionage, Tehran rejects Kuwaiti accusations, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: BRICS foreign ministers convene in Delhi
threads.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi arrived in New Delhi for the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting, with Israeli press framing the gathering as overshadowed by the US-Israeli war on Iran. Jerusalem Post and Times of Israel noted the forum brings Iran and the UAE together and will test the bloc's ability to produce a joint statement.

threads.label: US-Iran deal positioning and Gulf alignment
threads.summary: The White House issued a Presidential Determination under NDAA §1245(d)(4)(B) and (C) on Iran oil-trade sanctions, while Israeli officials told CNN they fear Trump may strike a "bad deal" with Tehran. Iran International reported Tehran is looking to China for guarantees in any future US agreement; IRIB cited Middle East Eye quoting US Ambassador Huckabee telling Gulf states they must choose between Iran and Israel.

threads.label: Espionage cases and covert contacts
threads.summary: Iran executed Ehsan Afrashteh on accusations of spying for Mossad according to the judiciary's Mizan News, and the Jewish Chronicle reported a suspected IRGC agent offered a Briton £40,000 to kill a London-based journalist. Times of Israel cited reports that Mossad and Shin Bet chiefs secretly visited the UAE during the Iran war.

threads.label: Iran-Kuwait diplomatic row
threads.summary: IRIB reported Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected as "entirely unfounded" Kuwaiti claims that Tehran was planning hostile measures against Kuwait. Defa Press separately promoted a forthcoming film 'Tigers' dramatising a 1980s Iranian F-5 strike on a US base in Kuwait.

threads.label: Regime channels amplify Western war-cost coverage
threads.summary: Defa Press cited CNN reporting the Pentagon's latest estimate of the war with Iran at $29 billion, up from $25 billion two weeks earlier. IRIB amplified Economist and Financial Times pieces describing food-price shocks in the US, a one-third drop in Saudi oil exports, and Asian countries reverting to coal.

events.title_en: The Economist: Prolongation of Iran crisis could inflict irreparable harm on Persian Gulf littoral states
events.summary_en: The Economist: Prolongation of Iran crisis could inflict irreparable harm on Persian Gulf littoral states. The Gulf Cooperation Council countries have thus far spent tens of billions of dollars from their economies to manage this crisis, but as weeks pass and turn into months, the risk of long-term damage increases. Saudi Arabia's oil exports have declined by approximately one-third since the war began, while Emirates' exports have halved. Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar have seen virtually no exports. In Dubai, hotel occupancy rates are estimated to have fallen to 10 percent.

events.title_en: Amir Valipanah: The people were the constant concern of the late commander Mousavi
events.summary_en: Amir Valipanah: The people were the constant concern of the late commander Mousavi. Brigadier General Hossein Valipanah, adviser to the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, whilst referring to cognitive warfare, stated: In the past war, war was difficult and this subject has taken root in the minds of the general public. Currently, however, the method of wars has changed and enemies seek to achieve their objectives without using hard and physical weapons. In fact, they want to achieve their goals through psychological operations and soft measures. They create rumours, establish a psychological atmosphere and achieve their aims without firing a single shot. This method is in fact called cognitive warfare.

events.title_en: Bloomberg: France's unemployment rate reached above 8 percent for the first time in five years
events.summary_en: Bloomberg: France's unemployment rate reached above 8 percent for the first time in five years. This figure dealt a severe blow to government promises regarding employment and is indicative of a slowdown in the labour market of Europe's second-largest economy. Reduced consumer demand and high interest rates have caused companies to refrain from hiring new staff and layoffs in industrial sectors have increased. According to a French statistics office report, unemployment among young people under 25 has grown at a faster rate and approached 18 percent.

events.title_en: Surveillance of Starlink users by the Zionist regime
events.summary_en: Surveillance of Starlink users by the Zionist regime. A Haaretz investigation shows that two Israeli companies, through developing technology, have been able to identify the location of Starlink users and in some cases their user information. These companies map the location of Starlink terminals worldwide and disclose the locations of those connecting to the internet through these devices. According to Haaretz, these companies can locate satellite communication devices, monitor the number of devices connected to each base station and identify users through their mobile phone numbers or associated social media accounts.

events.title_en: US Ambassador to occupied territories tells Persian Gulf states: You must choose between Iran and Israel
events.summary_en: US Ambassador to occupied territories tells Persian Gulf states: You must choose between Iran and Israel. Middle East Eye reported: Mike Huckabee (US Ambassador to Israel) warned Arab states bordering the Persian Gulf that they must choose between aligning with Iran or pursuing strategic cooperation with Israel and the United States. According to Huckabee, the US will not grant former military or economic benefits to countries that continue to seek diplomatic proximity with Iran. These statements demonstrate a serious shift in US foreign policy and pressure on traditional allies to fully align with Tel Aviv's strategies.

events.title_en: War with Iran would return the world to the coal age: The British Financial Times newspaper reported: Supply disruptions have caused many countries, particularly in Asia, to turn to coal use to the point that in recent months coal has become the largest shipment by volume for medium-sized vessels.
events.summary_en: War with Iran would return the world to the coal age. The British Financial Times newspaper reported: Supply disruptions have caused many countries, particularly in Asia, to turn to coal use to the point that in recent months coal has become the largest shipment by volume for medium-sized vessels. This trend shows that in conditions of energy disruption, some countries are reverting to the use of fuels such as coal; because access to oil and gas has become more difficult or expensive.

events.summary_en: Daily fuel savings of 20 million litres with public participation. National Oil Products Distribution Company CEO Karamati Vis-Karami: If every household in the country reduces its daily petrol consumption by just one litre, given approximately 20 million households, approximately 20 million litres of petrol will be saved daily. There are currently no concerns regarding sustainable fuel supply to the country, but consumption management must be prioritised. 1.5 billion litres reduction in oil and gas consumption in 1404. Through consumption management across different sectors, last year 1.5 billion litres were saved in oil and gas consumption, which resulted in zero imports and 1 billion dollars in foreign exchange savings.

events.title_en: The Economist: America faces a new food price shock
events.summary_en: The Economist: America faces a new food price shock. Currently, the greatest pressure from the Iran war on US food prices is seen in two stages of food packaging and transport in the supply chain. A large portion of food packaging is plastic, which itself is produced from oil. Petrochemical raw materials have now become approximately 40 percent more expensive. Additionally, 80 to 90 percent of American food products are transported by truck. With rising fuel prices, getting food to shop shelves has become significantly more expensive and this process will continue.

events.title_en: Chief Prosecutor of Bushehr province: 90,000 litres of smuggled diesel discovered at Rig Port
events.summary_en: Chief Prosecutor of Bushehr province: 90,000 litres of smuggled diesel discovered at Rig Port. Chief Prosecutor of Bushehr province: In pursuit of combating fuel smuggling and protecting national resources, through issuing judicial orders and coordinated action by naval and FRAJA forces, 90,000 litres of smuggled diesel were discovered. This operation was carried out following precise monitoring and surveillance at Rig Port and operational forces succeeded in seizing this shipment of smuggled fuel. A legal file has been opened in this regard and necessary measures to identify and deal with those involved are being pursued.

events.title_en: CNN: The final cost of war against Iran is one trillion dollars
events.summary_en: CNN: The final cost of war against Iran is one trillion dollars. The American media reported: The Pentagon in its latest estimate announced that the war with Iran has cost America 29 billion dollars to date. The new estimate exceeds the Pentagon's 25 billion dollar estimate presented to Congress two weeks ago. CNN cited unofficial estimates outside the US government as being much higher than these official government estimates and wrote: A scholar at the Kennedy School of Governance at Harvard University said in April that this conflict could ultimately cost American taxpayers one trillion dollars.

events.title_en: Poland's interest in US early warning aircraft
events.summary_en: Poland's interest in US early warning aircraft. Given Eastern European security tensions, Poland is seeking to strengthen its deterrence against potential forthcoming war through extensive overhaul of its air defence system. Poland, which commissioned two early warning and air control aircraft known as 'AWACS' in 2024, is now looking to replace them with a more advanced system. Poland is extensively restructuring its air defence architecture and given Eastern European security tensions is seeking to select systems that are both effective on the modern battlefield and fully compatible with advanced NATO equipment, particularly the F-35.

events.title_en: Cinema film 'Tigers' to be made depicting attack of two F-5 aircraft of Navy Air Force on American base
events.summary_en: Cinema film 'Tigers' to be made depicting attack of two F-5 aircraft of Navy Air Force on American base. The cinema film 'Tigers' depicting the historic and epic attack of two 'Sharkati Tiger F-5' fighter aircraft of the Army Air Force on the American Boehring base in Kuwait on the second day of the Third Imposed War will be produced, written by Mahdi Yazdani-khurram and produced by Habib Valinjad. Writing of this cinema work has commenced following completion of research and study periods. Further details about 'Tigers', which will be produced with direct support from the Army and particularly the Air Force, will be released soon.
